**1. The page.** The page opened. It is a blog called blog.biocomm.ai that reprints the full text of the Foreign Affairs essay "The AI Power Paradox", by Ian Bremmer and Mustafa Suleyman. The page gives the date as August 16, 2023. The sentence appears exactly as quoted:

The sentence just before it says that three years after GPT-3, open-source models matched its performance at one-sixtieth of the size. The page is not a news report; it reproduces the essay itself, so it counts as the authors' own words. Two things to note:
- It is a third-party copy. I did not check it against the original on foreignaffairs.com.
- The essay has two authors, so the words are Suleyman's together with Bremmer's.

The August 29 record presumably fixes a date by tying it to GPT-4-class models.
- **Part 4, a primary source:** Met, since the page reprints the essay itself.

**The overlap with the existing record.** The candidate and the recorded file make the same prediction: frontier-level models reach open source two to three years later. Under the restatement rule, a repeat of the same claim is filed under its first date. This essay is from August 16, earlier than the August 29 record. So the reviewer should decide whether to:
- add 2023-08-16 to that record as its first date, or
- treat the essay's general version as different from the GPT-4-specific one.
